head: b30597f49aad99032781c251b41a9de886cce3be
decision_summary: The successful public runTurn.nextState is the authoritative settled turn boundary. The scenario runner must not unconditionally rebuild and mutate that live state after success. A broad deletion is also unsupported because the scenario harness can create formations or apply control changes after runTurn and the retained project decision requires a final repair for those explicit topology-changing paths. Preserve the helper API and the dedicated final-save geometry projection; gate the scenario helper call only on a proven post-run topology invalidation.

immutable_public_turn_boundary.contract: A success result is returned only after the public war pipeline refreshes the front snapshot and passes the post-turn invariant barrier. Scenario, native, and desktop consumers must treat that successful nextState as settled unless a caller performs an explicit, separately-owned mutation.

established_findings.finding: On a cloned retained sealed T1 with correct operational edges, the current helper changes 190 leaves on its first pass and two on its second. The persisted changes are HVO sector threat_ratio and rs_22nd_krajina_infantry location_osid; the repeat pass moves the formation back. This is a live gameplay mutation, not artifact-only cleanup.

corps_front_sectors, formation sector assignment, assigned_sub_segment_id, and formation location are persisted gameplay state. Only the five named caches, including sector_combat_ratings, are disposable.

After runTurn, the scenario runner resolves headless opportunities, can create OOB formations, can apply control-flip proposals, and can apply baseline displacement before the repair call. OOB creation and applied political-control changes can invalidate formation/front/sector topology, so deleting the repair call for every path would be blind.
Final save uses a separate operational-edge projection, an explicit final-save reconciliation session, and a seal. That path is outside this proposal and must remain unchanged.

No evidence shows a public runTurn invariant defect. The public war pipeline already performs session-owned reconciliation/distribution/sealing and the post-turn barrier. Moving the scenario helper into runTurn would change native and desktop behavior without an established engine defect.

why_retained_capture_is_insufficient: The retained actual capture is from predecessor head 295d5f7290b1085dc76bbebb41df72386cd6b705, not current b30597f49aad99032781c251b41a9de886cce3be.
It captured PRE_REPAIR after scenario-owned handlers, not the immediate runTurn.nextState, so it cannot attribute pre-helper changes to the caller layer.

Its postcheck failed FINAL_NOT_EXACT_TO_COMPOSITE_AND_OBSERVER and ENTRY_EXACTNESS_FLAGS_FALSE. The retained state remains useful for the offline non-identity proof but cannot approve a current runtime boundary change.
The current diagnostic attempt selected no test and loaded no state; it is not boundary evidence.

mandatory_preimplementation_gate.scope: One current-head, exact one-week, real scenario-harness capture; one attempt; no campaign, replay, native, package, full suite, or retry.
capture_points: A: successful runTurn.nextState immediately after assertTurnSuccess and before any scenario-only mutation
B: the same live state immediately before repairScenarioArtifactState after all scenario-only handlers
C: the same live state immediately after repairScenarioArtifactState
required_receipts: HEAD, exact argv/selectors, operational graph identity/hash, child/wrapper exits, timeout status
canonical persisted-state hashes and runtime-state hashes at A/B/C
complete deterministic leaf diffs A->B and B->C, with disposable-cache paths separately classified
runTurn success/invariant status and final-sector reconciliation session/seal diagnostics
explicit counts/results for OOB creation and control-flip application
mandatory_preimplementation_gate.pass_condition: For an ordinary week with zero topology-changing scenario mutations, A and B are equal on persisted gameplay fields, and B->C demonstrates only the currently suspected unwanted rebuild effects. If A->B contains a topology mutation, the capture must identify its owning caller and the proposal must gate repair on that explicit mutation result rather than on week number or artifact emission.
mandatory_preimplementation_gate.stop_condition: Any selector/startup/capture-integrity failure stops the attempt; preserve it and do not treat it as proof or retry without a corrected, newly justified selector.

smallest_supported_implementation_after_: Keep repairScenarioArtifactState exported and keep its focused synthetic explicit-use coverage.

At the scenario call site only, replace the unconditional invocation with an explicit deterministic topology-dirty condition derived from actual post-run mutation results. Formation creation and applied control flips are candidate dirty owners; the boundary capture and function contracts must establish the final set.

When the condition is false, weekly reports, replay/checkpoint output, weekly saves, and the diagnostic observer consume the successful public nextState without another displacement/reconciliation pass.
When the condition is true, retain operational OSID edges and perform the scenario-owned repair before artifacts; do not change mechanics, data, thresholds, graph domains, or sector algorithms.
Leave the dedicated final-save geometry projection/session/seal unchanged.
forbidden_regressions: No change inside runTurn, war-phase reconciliation, displacement mechanics, sector construction, public native/desktop behavior, or save schema.
No broad removal of the helper, its explicit artifact use, or the final-save projection.
No sessionless clean-path rebuild of an already settled public nextState.
No stale or empty operational fronts/sectors, enemy-territory active formation, observer/save divergence, wrong SID/OSID graph, or canonical serialization of disposable caches.
No coefficient, threshold, authored data, baseline, acceptance criterion, or calibration tuning change.
required_postimplementation_verification: Focused RED/GREEN characterization of the A/B/C boundary on current head.
Clean-path one-week parity: persisted gameplay state at artifact boundary equals the successful public nextState; weekly save, observer, replay/checkpoint state agree.
Dirty-path tests for actual OOB formation creation and applied control flips: repair occurs once, with operational edges, and yields valid persisted sectors/assignments.
Existing explicit helper displacement test remains green; repeated repair is not invoked on the clean path.
Final-save operational projection/session/seal and save-load validation remain green.
Affected scenario-harness, turn-invariant, sector persistence, serialization, determinism, and TypeScript checks pass before any calibration run.

Because this changes a territory/calibration trajectory, a final qualifying candidate still requires the authorized 188-week calibration gate and full suite under the existing acceptance criteria; focused proof cannot waive them.

required_for_narrow_change: engine/systems and canon-compliance review of the public boundary and persisted sector/location contract
scope_escalation_triggers: Any edit to runTurn, war phases, displacement, sector construction, public native/desktop consumers, save schema, or final-save projection requires a new engine/systems proposal and owner approval.
Any gameplay rule, coefficient, threshold, authored data, historical anchor, or acceptance-criterion change requires the applicable canon/calibration/history authority.
Any FORAWWV or sensitive-history change triggers its mandated panel; none is justified by this proposal.
